summary.text: Planck was a European Space Agency observatory that ran from 2009 to 2013 and mapped small variations in the cosmic microwave background.
It improved on earlier NASA observations from WMAP, with higher resolution and sensitivity and nine frequency bands instead of five.
Its data gave precise values for key cosmological parameters, including the age of the universe and the average density of ordinary and dark matter.

facts.label: Operator
facts.value: The European Space Agency, from 2009 to 2013

facts.label: Original name
facts.value: COBRAS/SAMBA, later renamed for Max Planck

facts.label: Full scans
facts.value: Five scans of the sky, against a target of two

items.prompt: A team wants to see whether a newer telescope can pick out features on much smaller scales than an older one. What did Planck offer over WMAP here?

options.label: Sharper detail, probing much smaller scales
Lower resolution but a longer-lasting mission
The same resolution but a much stronger signal
Fewer frequency bands but a much bigger mirror

items.explain: Planck had higher resolution and sensitivity than WMAP, which let it probe the power spectrum of the CMB to much smaller scales.

items.prompt: Why did Planck observe in nine frequency bands rather than the five used by WMAP?

options.label: To measure how old the probe itself was
To fill the space on a larger spacecraft
To improve the models of foreground sources
To avoid using any cooling systems

items.explain: More bands were meant to improve the astrophysical foreground models, since foreground subtraction limited most measurements.

items.prompt: A friend says Planck's measurements were limited mostly by weak detectors. According to what is expected, what limited them more?

options.label: How well foregrounds could be subtracted
The short length of the mission
The cost of launching it
The shape of its spacecraft body

items.explain: Most measurements are expected to be limited by how well foregrounds can be subtracted, rather than by detector performance or mission length.

items.prompt: Planck's high-frequency instrument stopped working soon after a particular supply ran out. What was that supply?

options.label: Fuel used to steer around the Sun
Helium-3 for its dilution refrigerator
Battery power for the radio link
Liquid nitrogen for the cold optics

items.explain: The on-board helium-3 supply for the dilution refrigerator was exhausted in January 2012, so the HFI would become unusable within days.

items.prompt: Of the six bands of Planck's high-frequency instrument, which can measure the polarisation of incoming radiation?

options.label: All six bands equally
Only the highest two bands
None of them
Only the lower four bands

items.explain: Only the lower four of the six bands can measure polarisation; the two higher bands cannot.

items.prompt: What happened to Planck at the end of its mission, to avoid endangering future missions?

options.label: It was brought back to Earth
Moved to a graveyard orbit around the Sun and passivated
It was left running at its observing post until it failed
It was sent down into the atmosphere to burn up

items.explain: It was put into a heliocentric graveyard orbit and passivated so it could not endanger future missions.
